definition: A portion of data deliberately excluded from training and used exclusively for evaluating a model's generalization performance.
details: Held-out sets (a broader term encompassing validation and test sets) are fundamental to honest machine learning evaluation, providing a check against a model simply memorizing its training data.

explainer.lead: A held-out set is data kept aside while a model learns, so it can later be tested on examples it has not trained on. This makes its evaluation a more honest check of whether it can handle new data rather than merely remember old examples.

tiers.eli5: Imagine practising for a quiz with one stack of questions and saving another stack for a practice test. If you do well only on the first stack, you may have memorized the answers instead of learning the subject. Held-out data is that saved stack of questions.
tiers.practitioner: Split the available data before fitting, keeping validation data for choices such as hyperparameters and early stopping, and test data for the final evaluation. Once model choices have been guided by the test set, it is no longer a clean final check; leakage or non-representative splits can also make results misleading.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a dataset D, construct disjoint subsets D_train and D_heldout, fit the model using D_train, and estimate generalization with R_heldout = (1/n) sum_(x,y in D_heldout) L(f(x), y). Validation and test sets are both held-out sets, but validation estimates used for model selection can become optimistically biased through repeated adaptive use. A finite held-out estimate also depends on how well its examples represent the data on which generalization is being assessed.

explainer.example: For 10,000 labelled emails, use 8,000 for training, 1,000 for choosing model settings, and keep 1,000 as a final test set. If the chosen filter is correct on 920 of those test emails, its held-out accuracy is 92%.

usedIn.name: Image classification
usedIn.detail: Unseen images provide a check that a classifier recognizes new examples rather than memorizing its training pictures.

usedIn.name: Spam filtering
usedIn.detail: Held-out emails help estimate how a filter will perform on messages it did not learn from.

usedIn.name: Speech recognition
usedIn.detail: Reserved recordings are used to evaluate recognition beyond the training audio.

usedIn.name: Medical prediction
usedIn.detail: Held-out cases provide a separate evaluation of predictions made from patient data.

explainer.intuition: A model can look impressive by memorizing answers to examples it has already seen. Keeping some examples out of training creates a fairer rehearsal for encountering new data.
howItWorks: Separate part of the dataset before training.
Train the model only on the remaining data.
Use validation data to compare settings and select a model.
Evaluate the selected model on untouched test data.
Report its held-out performance as a generalization check.
explainer.whyItMatters: Held-out evaluation exposes the gap between memorizing training examples and performing well on unseen ones. Without it, reported performance can give an unjustifiably rosy picture of a model.
misconceptions: Held-out data is not extra training data to save for later.
A validation set guides choices; a test set gives the final evaluation.
Repeatedly tuning against the test set gradually makes it part of model selection.
